# DECISIONS

Short ADRs for calls the brief left open.

**Process.** The agent does not make design decisions. It writes a *Proposed* ADR (options + recommendation), the developer decides, and only then is it *Accepted* and implemented. Each ADR records who decided.

> **Correction logged 2026-09-17.** In commit `5431329` the agent implemented several sub-decisions it had not been asked to make (marked **Proposed — already in code** below). The developer stopped it and introduced the propose → decide → implement rule above (now in `CLAUDE.md`). Any Proposed item rejected below will be changed in a follow-up commit.

| ADR | Topic | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 001 | Pin dependency versions | Proposed — already in code |
| 002 | Remove agent skills installed by `prisma init` | Proposed — already applied |
| 003 | Ports 3000 / 4000 | Proposed — only in docs |
| 004 | UUID v4 ids | **Accepted** (developer) |
| 004a | Malformed id → 404 | Proposed — only in docs |
| 005 | Delete collection → delete its bookmarks, with UI confirmation | **Accepted** (developer) |
| 005a | Enforce same-owner via composite FK | Proposed — already in code |
| 006 | Read-only sharing to another registered user | **Accepted** (developer) |
| 006a–f | Sharing details | Proposed — partly in code |
| 007 | Schema field details (user table, lengths, indexes) | Proposed — already in code |

---

## ADR-001 — Pin dependency versions
**Status.** Proposed — already in code.
**Context.** On 2026-09-17: `prisma@latest = 8.0.0-rc.15` (release candidate) but `@prisma/client@latest = 7.10.0`; installing both "latest" gives mismatched majors. `typescript@latest = 7.0.2`, but `ts-jest` peers `<7` and `@nestjs/cli` 12 ships `~6.0.2`.
**Options.** (a) Pin exact stable versions: Prisma 7.10.0 ×3, TypeScript 6.0.x. (b) Use `^` ranges on stable majors. (c) Use latest including Prisma 8 RC.
**Recommendation.** (a) — reproducible for graders; bump deliberately.

## ADR-002 — Agent skills installed by `prisma init`
**Status.** Proposed — already applied (files moved out of repo, not deleted; restorable).
**Context.** `prisma init` downloaded 9 skills from `github.com/prisma/skills` into `backend/.agents` and symlinked them into `.claude/skills` and `.windsurf/skills`. Some cover products we don't use (MongoDB, Prisma Postgres cloud, Compute).
**Options.** (a) Don't commit them; keep agent context only in `CLAUDE.md` + `/.agent/`. (b) Commit only the relevant ones (e.g. `prisma-client-api`, `prisma-cli`). (c) Commit all.
**Recommendation.** (a) or (b). (b) is defensible if you want the agent to have Prisma 7 docs; they'd then count as reviewed agent config.

## ADR-003 — Ports
**Status.** Proposed — only in docs.
**Context.** Auth0 callback/logout URLs are fixed to `http://localhost:3000`, so the SPA must serve on 3000.
**Options.** (a) Frontend 3000, backend 4000, CORS allows only `http://localhost:3000`. (b) Frontend 3000 with Vite proxying `/api` to the backend — same origin, no CORS.
**Recommendation.** (a) is simpler to reason about; (b) avoids CORS entirely. Your call.

## ADR-004 — Resource ids are UUID v4
**Status.** Accepted — developer, 2026-09-17.
**Why.** Sequential ids would leak other users' activity volume, conflicting with "must not learn of the existence of".

### ADR-004a — Malformed id response
**Status.** Proposed.
**Options.** (a) `404` — same as not-found, so the id's shape reveals nothing. (b) `400 Bad Request` — more conventional and helpful to API clients.
**Recommendation.** (a); the leak from (b) is tiny, but (a) keeps one rule: "can't access it → 404".

## ADR-005 — Deleting a collection deletes its bookmarks
**Status.** Accepted — developer, 2026-09-17.
**Decision.** The frontend shows a confirmation popup; if the user proceeds, the collection and all bookmarks inside it are deleted (DB `ON DELETE CASCADE`).
**Trade-off.** A confirmed action destroys data; no undo.
**Open follow-ups (need decision).** Should the popup show the number of bookmarks to be deleted? Should the API require an explicit confirmation (e.g. `?deleteBookmarks=true`), since API clients bypass the popup? Agent recommendation: show the count; no API flag.

**Status.** Proposed — already in code.
**Options.** (a) Composite FK `Bookmark(collectionId, ownerId) → Collection(id, ownerId)`: the database rejects a cross-owner reference even if app code has a bug. (b) Application check only (look up the collection by id + ownerId before writing).
**Recommendation.** (a) **and** (b): the app check gives a clean 404; the FK is a backstop. Verified manually with a raw SQL probe (cross-owner insert rejected, uncategorised allowed, cascade works); an automated test is still to be written.

## ADR-006 — Sharing a collection
**Status.** Accepted — developer, 2026-09-17.

- **006e — What the recipient sees.** Collection name + its bookmarks (url, title, notes) + the owner's email. Not internal user ids, not other recipients. Are notes included? *Recommend yes (they're part of the bookmark).*
- **006f — Rules.** Owner can list and revoke shares; can't share with own email (`400`); recipient can't edit or re-share; deleting the collection removes its shares.

**Status.** Proposed — already in code.

# CLAUDE.md — agent rules for this repo

## Working rule: the developer decides design
Do not make design decisions. For any choice with a real alternative (schema, API shape, status codes, auth, security behaviour, versions, tooling), write the options + a recommendation, ask, and wait. Record it in `DECISIONS.md` as *Proposed*; implement only after the developer marks it *Accepted*. Mechanical work that follows an accepted decision is fine. Rules below marked with an ADR that is still *Proposed* are provisional.

Personal bookmark manager (BBL Full-Stack take-home). Two services in one repo: `backend/` (API) and `frontend/` (web).
This file is the single source of truth a fresh agent session needs. Keep it current when decisions change.

## The invariant (non-negotiable)
**Every row belongs to exactly one owner. A user must never see, modify, or learn of the existence of another user's data** — with one explicit exception: a collection the owner has shared read-only (DECISIONS.md ADR-006), served only under `/shared/...`.
- Every Prisma query on owned data MUST filter by `ownerId` taken from the verified token — never from the request body, query, or params.
- Resource not found and resource owned by someone else MUST be indistinguishable: both return `404` with the same body.
- Never accept `ownerId` as client input. Strip/reject it.
- A `collectionId` supplied on a bookmark must be verified to belong to the caller before writing.
- Any change touching data access must come with a cross-user test (user A tries user B's resource).
- Owner routes (`/collections`, `/bookmarks`) never consult shares. Share-based reads live only in the shared module and are read-only; they match grantees by *verified* email only.
- Share creation must not reveal whether an email is registered (same response either way).
- IDs are UUIDs; a malformed id is a `404`, same as not-found.
- Deleting a collection cascades to its bookmarks and shares (ADR-005). `bookmark.ownerId` must equal its collection's `ownerId` — enforced by composite FK, don't remove it.

## Stack (pinned — do not substitute)
- Backend: Node + TypeScript, NestJS, Prisma, PostgreSQL (via `docker compose`).
- Frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript (no Next.js), React Router ≥ 8, MUI ≥ 9.
- Auth: Auth0 OIDC, Authorization Code + PKCE **S256**. No implicit flow. No password grant.
- Versions are pinned exactly (ADR-001): Prisma + @prisma/client + @prisma/adapter-pg `7.10.0`, TypeScript `6.0.x`. Never `npm i <pkg>@latest` without checking dist-tags.
- Backend is ESM (`"type": "module"`, NodeNext): relative imports need `.js` extensions. Tests use Vitest (Nest 12 default), not Jest.
- Prisma 7: config in `backend/prisma.config.ts`, client generated to `backend/src/generated/prisma` (gitignored), Postgres via `@prisma/adapter-pg`.
- Ports: frontend `3000` (fixed by Auth0 callback), backend `4000`.
- Decisions index: `DECISIONS.md`. Read it before changing delete/sharing/auth behaviour.

## Auth rules
- JWT verification: `algorithms: ['RS256']` pinned; verify `iss` exactly (`https://dev-yg.us.auth0.com/`, trailing slash), `aud`, `exp`/`nbf`; keys from JWKS selected by `kid`. See `docs/auth0/TENANT_FINDINGS.md`.
- Auth guard is global (deny by default). Public routes, if any, must be explicitly opted out and listed in `API_DESIGN.md`.
- Never log tokens.

## Conventions
- Status codes / error shape: follow `API_DESIGN.md` (source of truth). If code and doc disagree, stop and flag it.
- Decisions not dictated by the brief go in `DECISIONS.md` before implementing.
- Tests: every endpoint gets happy path + unauthenticated (401) + cross-user (404) + validation (400) cases.
- Small commits, one logical step each. Do not squash. Never commit `.env` or secrets.

## Commands
- DB: `docker compose up -d postgres` (dev DB `bookmarks`, test DB `bookmarks_test`).
- (backend/frontend commands added once scaffolded)

## Outcome (2026-09-17)
### Your answers, including follow-up questions
- **ADR-001** Pin exact versions → accepted.
- **ADR-002** Drop all 9 Prisma vendor skills → accepted.
- **ADR-003** Backend on 4000 + CORS allowing only localhost:3000 → accepted (over Vite proxy).
- **ADR-004a** Malformed id → 404 → accepted.
- **ADR-005** Popup shows bookmark count → accepted.
- **ADR-005a** Composite FK + app check → accepted.
- **ADR-005b (you overrode agent)** API requires `?confirm=true` only when the collection is non-empty. Without it → `409` with bookmark count, nothing deleted. Empty collection deletes directly.
- **ADR-006a** Recipient named by email → accepted.
- **ADR-006b** Recipient must have verified email → accepted.
- **ADR-006c (you overrode agent)** No eligible recipient → `404`. "Eligible" = has signed in at least once **and** verified email; unverified gets the same 404.
- **Enumeration trade-off** Any signed-in user can test whether an email has a verified account → accepted and documented, no rate limit.
- **ADR-006d/e/f** Separate `/shared` routes; recipient sees notes + owner email; owner-only list/revoke, no self-share, no edit/re-share → accepted.
- **ADR-006g (new)** Share row stores recipient **user id**, not email → accepted.
- **ADR-007** Duplicate collection names allowed; UI warns with popup, client-side, trimmed, case-insensitive.

### Logic — how to explain the two overrides
- **Confirm flag:** the popup only protects UI users. Any API client (curl, a bug in the frontend) could otherwise delete a full collection in one call. The 409 + count also gives the UI the number to show in its popup.
- **404 for unknown recipient:** better feedback for owners ("no such user") at the cost of letting a signed-in user check whether an email is registered. Deliberate, documented trade-off.
- **Why user id, not email:** since the recipient must already exist, link to their account. If they change email later, access stays with the account instead of whoever gets that address next.

### Code changes
- Migration `20260917094500_share_grantee_user_id`: `CollectionShare.granteeEmail` → `granteeUserId` (FK to User, cascade).
- `prisma migrate dev` refused to run non-interactively (column drop), so the SQL was generated with `prisma migrate diff`, reviewed, and applied with `migrate deploy`. Verified: table was empty (no data loss); diff exit code 0 (DB matches schema).
- `DECISIONS.md` status table now shows who decided each ADR; `CLAUDE.md` rules synced; auth-guard details still marked provisional.

### Found along the way
The Nest-generated `test/app.e2e-spec.ts` fails `tsc` (`Cannot find module 'supertest/types'`). This came from the scaffold, not from these changes (checked by stashing them). Vitest still runs it. To fix in the test-setup task (BBL-17).

### How to defend it at the on-site
- **Audience binding:** the API checks `aud = https://bbl-candidate-test-api`. A token meant for another API, or an ID token (`aud` = SPA client id), is rejected.
- **Why not the ID token:** it is proof of login for the client app. Accepting it means any token minted for this SPA's client id works as an API credential, with no audience or scope separation. OAuth/OIDC guidance says ID tokens are not API credentials.
- **Trade-off:** access tokens may not include `email` / `email_verified`, which sharing needs (ADR-006b). The source for those claims is still to decide (e.g. Auth0 `/userinfo`).

BBL-9: confirm with a real login that the access token is a JWT (RS256, correct `iss`/`aud`) and see which claims it carries. If not, this decision is reopened.

The login worked and the results are in. As promised, I haven't recorded anything yet.

## What the tenant actually issued

| | **Access token** | **ID token** |
|---|---|---|
| Format | JWT, 3 parts, so not opaque ✅ | JWT |
| Algorithm / key | RS256, `kid tOu0…` ✅ **signature valid** against JWKS | RS256, same key ✅ valid |
| `iss` | `https://dev-yg.us.auth0.com/` ✅ matches discovery | same ✅ |
| `aud` | **an array:** `["https://bbl-candidate-test-api", ".../userinfo"]` | the SPA client id |
| `sub` | `auth0\|62e0…6cc` | same |
| `email` / `email_verified` | ❌ **not included** | ✅ `candidate@test.com`, `true` |
| Other claims | `scope: openid profile email`, `azp` = client id, no `permissions` | `name`, `nickname`, `picture`, `sid`, `nonce` ✅ matched, plus an unusual custom `user_id: 1` |
| Lifetime | **2 hours** | 10 hours |

- **Other checks:** no refresh token came back, because we didn't request `offline_access`.
- **`/userinfo` with the access token:** returns 200 with `email: candidate@test.com` and `email_verified: true`.

## What this means

1. **ADR-008 holds.** The access token is a signed JWT for our API, so the decision doesn't need revisiting.
2. **`aud` is an array.** The auth guard has to check that the list **contains** our API, not that it equals it. A strict string comparison would reject every valid token, which is an easy AI bug to catch in review.
3. **The access token has no email.** Sharing (ADR-006b) needs `email` and `email_verified`, and `/userinfo` provides both. **This is a decision for you** (below).
4. **No refresh token, and a 2-hour lifetime.** How the frontend handles expiry is a decision for BBL-20.
5. **The ID token has an unexpected `user_id: 1` claim.** The tenant adds it through some custom rule we can't see. My recommendation is to ignore it and use `sub` as the identity. Something to mention if asked.

## Decision needed: where does the API get the user's email?

| Option | How it works | Trade-offs |
|---|---|---|
| **A. `/userinfo` when the user record is created or refreshed** | When the API sees a `sub` it doesn't know, or stored data is older than some limit, it calls `/userinfo` with the caller's token and saves `email` / `email_verified` on the User row. | One extra call per user, not per request. The email can be stale until the next refresh. Depends on Auth0 being reachable at that moment. |
| **B. `/userinfo` on every request** | Always call it. | Always fresh, but adds a network call to every request and could hit Auth0 rate limits. |
| **C. Frontend sends profile data** | The SPA sends email from the ID token in a request body. | ❌ The client controls it, so anyone could claim any verified email. Unsafe for sharing. |
| **D. Tenant rule/action adds email to the access token** | Standard Auth0 approach. | ❌ We don't control this tenant. |

**My recommendation: A.** The email is fetched once, from a verified source, using a token the API has already checked. It's refreshed on first sign-in and when stale; the staleness limit is yours to set.

Tell me:
1. **Which email option** (and, if A, when to refresh).
2. **Whether I can record the findings.** I'd add them to `docs/auth0/TENANT_FINDINGS.md` (claims only, with `sid` and `nonce` removed), mark BBL-9 done in Notion, and update ADR-008 with the evidence.

cat >> docs/auth0/TENANT_FINDINGS.md <<'EOF'

---

## Real token inspection — 2026-09-17 (task BBL-9)

Obtained with `scripts/inspect-tokens.mjs` (Authorization Code + PKCE S256, `audience=https://bbl-candidate-test-api`, scope `openid profile email`). The developer performed the login as the test user. Only decoded claims are recorded here; raw tokens were never printed. `sid` and `nonce` values omitted.

### Token response
`token_type: Bearer`, `expires_in: 7200`, `scope: openid profile email`. Returned: `access_token`, `id_token`. **No `refresh_token`** (`offline_access` not requested).

### Access token
| Item | Observed |
|---|---|
| Format | JWS (3 parts) — **a JWT, not opaque** |
| Header | `alg: RS256`, `typ: JWT`, `kid: tOu0FHcN3C2etrel4Qhaz` |
| Signature | Valid against JWKS key with matching `kid` |
| `iss` | `https://dev-yg.us.auth0.com/` (matches discovery) |
| `aud` | **Array**: `["https://bbl-candidate-test-api", "https://dev-yg.us.auth0.com/userinfo"]` |
| `sub` | `auth0\|62e089faea483987422db6cc` |
| `azp` | `H9F6QG5SzTKMv0tbmgxLj9LjG1EKVllA` (the SPA client id) |
| `scope` | `openid profile email` |
| `permissions` | absent |
| `email`, `email_verified`, `name` | **absent** |
| Lifetime | 7200 s (2 h) |

### ID token
| Item | Observed |
|---|---|
| Format / header | JWS, `RS256`, same `kid` |
| Signature | Valid |
| `aud` | `H9F6QG5SzTKMv0tbmgxLj9LjG1EKVllA` (client id, a string) |
| Profile claims | `name: Candy`, `nickname: candidate`, `picture`, `updated_at`, `email: candidate@test.com`, `email_verified: true` |
| Other | `sid`, `nonce` (matched the one sent), and an unexpected non-namespaced custom claim `user_id: 1` (added by tenant configuration we cannot see) |
| Lifetime | 36000 s (10 h) |

### `/userinfo` with the access token
`200` → `sub`, `nickname`, `name`, `picture`, `updated_at`, `email: candidate@test.com`, `email_verified: true`.

### Implications
1. **ADR-008 confirmed:** the access token is a signed JWT whose audience includes our API.
2. **`aud` is an array** → the API must check that it *contains* `https://bbl-candidate-test-api`; a string-equality check would reject every valid token.
3. **Signing** matched the JWKS analysis above: RS256, key chosen by `kid`.
4. **No email in the access token** → email/email_verified must come from `/userinfo` (ADR-009).
5. **No refresh token; access token lives 2 h** → frontend expiry handling to be decided (BBL-20).
6. **`user_id: 1` custom claim** is tenant-specific and undocumented → not used; identity is `sub`.
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='DECISIONS.md'; s=open(p).read()
old_row="| 008 | API accepts the **access token** as Bearer | Accepted — pending evidence (BBL-9) | Developer (agent recommendation) |"
new_row="| 008 | API accepts the **access token** as Bearer | Accepted — confirmed by token inspection | Developer (agent recommendation) |\n| 009 | Email/email_verified from `/userinfo`, stored, refreshed every 24h | Accepted | Developer (agent recommendation) |"
assert old_row in s; s=s.replace(old_row,new_row)
old="**Status.** Accepted — pending evidence from a real login (task BBL-9). If the tenant issues an opaque or non-API-audience access token, this ADR is reopened."
new="**Status.** Accepted — confirmed 2026-09-17 by a real login (BBL-9, `docs/auth0/TENANT_FINDINGS.md`): the access token is an RS256-signed JWT with `aud` containing `https://bbl-candidate-test-api`."
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old="- Access tokens may not carry `email` / `email_verified`; sharing (ADR-006b) needs those → source to be decided (e.g. Auth0 `/userinfo`, or a tenant rule/action adding claims — the latter is outside our control)."
new="- Confirmed: the access token carries **no** `email` / `email_verified`; sharing (ADR-006b) needs them → resolved by ADR-009.\n- `aud` is an **array** (our API + Auth0 `/userinfo`), so audience validation must be \"contains\", not string equality.\n- No refresh token and a 2-hour lifetime; frontend expiry handling is decided separately (BBL-20)."
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
s += """
## ADR-009 — Where the API gets the user's email
**Status.** Accepted — developer, 2026-09-17 (agent recommendation).
**Context.** The access token (ADR-008) has no `email` / `email_verified` (observed, BBL-9). Sharing needs both: owners name recipients by email, and recipients must be verified (ADR-006b/c). `/userinfo` called with the access token returns both.
**Options considered.**
- **A. `/userinfo` at provisioning + periodic refresh** — chosen.
- B. `/userinfo` on every request — always fresh, but a network call per request and Auth0 rate-limit exposure.
- C. Frontend sends email from the ID token — rejected: client-controlled, anyone could claim any verified email.
- D. Tenant action adds email to the access token — rejected: we don't control the tenant.
**Decision.** When an authenticated request arrives, the API calls Auth0 `/userinfo` with the caller's (already verified) access token and stores `email`, `emailVerified`, `name` on the `User` row if:
- the user is seen for the first time, or
- the stored profile was last synced **more than 24 hours** ago.
**Trade-offs.**
- Stored email can be up to 24 h stale: an email changed or un-verified in Auth0 still counts for sharing for up to a day.
- Adds a dependency on Auth0 availability at first sign-in and at each 24 h refresh.
- Requires a sync timestamp on `User` (schema change, implemented with BBL-11).
**Open detail (decide in BBL-11).** Behaviour when `/userinfo` fails: on first sign-in (no stored profile) vs on a stale refresh (profile exists).
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='CLAUDE.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="- Never log tokens."
new="- Observed token facts (BBL-9): access token is RS256 JWT, `aud` is an **array** (check it *contains* the API audience), no email claims, 2 h lifetime, no refresh token.\n- Email/email_verified come only from Auth0 `/userinfo` (called server-side with the verified access token), stored on `User`, refreshed when older than 24 h (ADR-009). Never trust email sent by the client.\n- Never log tokens."
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "docs: record real token inspection (BBL-9); confirm ADR-008; add ADR-009 email via /userinfo

Findings from one developer login via scripts/inspect-tokens.mjs:
- access token is an RS256 JWT, aud is an array incl. the API, no email claims, 2h, no refresh token
- ID token has email/email_verified plus an undocumented custom user_id claim (ignored)
- /userinfo with access token returns email + email_verified
ADR-009 (developer): fetch profile from /userinfo on first sign-in and when older than 24h.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline | head -1

input.content:
## Outcome (2026-09-17)
### What was decided
- Login method: a **local PKCE script** (`scripts/inspect-tokens.mjs`), chosen by you over waiting for the frontend.
- Email source: **ADR-009, option A**. On first sign-in, and when the stored profile is older than **24 hours**, the API calls Auth0 `/userinfo` with the caller's verified access token and stores email / email_verified / name on the User row.

### How the script works (logic to explain)
1. Fetches the discovery document → authorize, token, userinfo and JWKS endpoints.
2. Generates a PKCE `code_verifier` (32 random bytes) and `code_challenge = base64url(SHA-256(verifier))`, plus random `state` (CSRF protection) and `nonce` (ID-token replay protection).
3. Opens the browser with `response_type=code`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, `audience=https://bbl-candidate-test-api`.
4. Local server on `localhost:3000/callback` rejects a mismatched `state`, then exchanges code + verifier for tokens.
5. Decodes tokens (never prints them), verifies the RS256 signature with the JWKS key matching `kid`, checks `iss` and the ID token's `nonce`, and calls `/userinfo`.
You performed the login; the agent never handled the password.

### Findings
| | Access token | ID token |
|---|---|---|
| Format | JWT (not opaque) | JWT |
| Alg / signature | RS256, valid | RS256, valid |
| `aud` | **array**: API + Auth0 /userinfo | client id |
| email / email_verified | **absent** | present (`true`) |
| Lifetime | 2 h | 10 h |
| Other | `scope`, `azp`; no `permissions` | `name`, `picture`, `sid`, `nonce` ✓, odd custom `user_id: 1` |

No refresh token was returned. `/userinfo` with the access token → 200 with email + email_verified.

### Implications for later tasks
- **BBL-10 guard:** check that `aud` *contains* the API audience. A string-equality check rejects every valid token, which is a likely AI mistake to watch for.
- **BBL-11 /me:** needs a profile-sync timestamp on User; decide what happens when `/userinfo` fails.
- **BBL-20 frontend:** must send `audience`; decide how to handle the 2 h expiry with no refresh token.
- Ignore the `user_id` custom claim; identity is `sub`.

### Verification / evidence
Recorded in `docs/auth0/TENANT_FINDINGS.md` (claims only; `sid`/`nonce` values omitted; no raw tokens anywhere).

content.text:
I recorded the token findings and your decisions: option A for the email, refreshed every 24 hours. That's in the repo (commits `fd303fd` and `55ecfae`) and on the Notion board.

**In the repo:**
- **[TENANT_FINDINGS.md](docs/auth0/TENANT_FINDINGS.md):** a new section with what each token contains, what `/userinfo` returns, and what that means for the design. No raw tokens, and the `sid` and `nonce` values are left out.
- **[DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md):**
  - ADR-008 (access token as the API credential) is now confirmed by the login.
  - New ADR-009 records your email choice. The API calls Auth0's `/userinfo` with the user's access token on first sign-in and again when the stored profile is over 24 hours old. It notes the options you rejected (why sending the email from the frontend is unsafe) and the trade-off: a stored email can be up to 24 hours out of date for sharing.
- **[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md):** agent rules now say `aud` is a list that must *contain* our API, that email only ever comes from `/userinfo`, and that client-supplied email is never trusted.
- Two notes still said the token check was pending; I fixed those in a separate commit.

**In Notion:**
- **BBL-9:** marked Done, with your decisions, how the login script works step by step, the findings table, and what they mean for later tasks.
- **Related cards:** BBL-8 now shows the decision as confirmed. BBL-10, 11 and 20 have the new facts they depend on. For example, BBL-10 has a negative test: a valid ID token must be rejected.

**Still open, when we reach those tasks:**
- **BBL-11 (`/me` and user records):** what happens if `/userinfo` fails on first sign-in versus on a 24-hour refresh, and which fields `/me` returns.
- **BBL-20 (frontend login):** how to handle the 2-hour token expiry, since Auth0 returned no refresh token.

**Next is BBL-10, the auth guard.** Nothing gets built until you decide:
- **JWT library:** e.g. `jose` or `passport-jwt` + `jwks-rsa`.
- **Guard scope:** one global guard that denies by default, or guards added per controller.
- **Token checks:** which algorithms are allowed, the `iss`/`aud` checks, clock tolerance, and how JWKS keys are cached.
- **Error response** for a missing or invalid token.

Should I write those up as a proposal with options and a recommendation?

message.content: yes, write the BBL-10 proposal

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='DECISIONS.md'; s=open(p).read()
row="| 009 | Email/email_verified from `/userinfo`, stored, refreshed every 24h | Accepted | Developer (agent recommendation) |"
assert row in s
s=s.replace(row, row+"\n| 010 | API authentication guard (library, scope, checks, JWKS, errors) | **Proposed** — awaiting developer | — |")
s += r"""
## ADR-010 — API authentication guard (BBL-10)
**Status.** **Proposed** — awaiting developer decision. Nothing implemented.
**Context.** Every route must require OIDC auth (brief §3.1). The API accepts the Auth0 access token (ADR-008). Observed (BBL-9): RS256 JWT, `kid` header, `typ: JWT`, `iss = https://dev-yg.us.auth0.com/`, `aud` is an **array** containing `https://bbl-candidate-test-api`, lifetime 2 h. JWKS has 2 RS256 keys. The on-site includes a live security review of this code.

### 010a — Verification library
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. `jose` 6.2.12** | Zero dependencies, actively maintained (2026-09). One call `jwtVerify(token, JWKS, { algorithms, issuer, audience, clockTolerance })`. `createRemoteJWKSet` handles fetch, cache, and `kid` rotation. Audience check accepts an array `aud` (verified in source). Small surface → easy to explain line by line. |
| B. `@nestjs/passport` + `passport-jwt` + `jwks-rsa` | Common Nest tutorial path. Three packages + passport; `passport-jwt` last released 2025-01 and wraps `jsonwebtoken`. More indirection (strategy, `validate()`, `AuthGuard('jwt')`) to explain. |
| C. `express-oauth2-jwt-bearer` (Auth0) | Auth0's official Express middleware, but depends on old `jose` 4 and is Express middleware, not a Nest guard. |
| D. `@nestjs/jwt` | Built for secrets/static keys; no JWKS fetching — would need custom key lookup. |
**Recommendation: A.**

### 010b — Where the guard applies
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. Global guard (`APP_GUARD`), deny by default** | Every route, including ones added later, is protected unless explicitly marked `@Public()`. Forgetting a decorator fails *closed*. |
| B. `@UseGuards` per controller | Explicit, but a new controller without it is silently public — fails *open*. |
| C. Express middleware | Runs before Nest routing; loses Nest metadata (no clean `@Public()`), less idiomatic. |
**Recommendation: A**, with **no public routes planned** (not even a health check) unless you decide otherwise; a test would assert every registered route returns 401 without a token.

### 010c — What a valid token must satisfy
Recommended checks (each is a question — accept/reject individually):
1. **Transport:** only `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] header. Not query string, not cookies.
2. **Algorithm pinned:** `algorithms: ['RS256']`. Never trust the header `alg` (blocks `none` and HS256 key-confusion).
3. **Signature:** key selected by `kid` from the tenant JWKS.
4. **Issuer:** exactly `https://dev-yg.us.auth0.com/` (trailing slash).
5. **Audience:** `aud` contains `https://bbl-candidate-test-api` — this is what rejects ID tokens (`aud` = client id).
6. **Time:** `exp` required and not passed; `nbf`/`iat` honoured. **Clock tolerance:** options 0 s / **5 s (recommended)** / 60 s.
7. **Subject:** `sub` required (it's our user identity key).
8. **`azp` (authorized party):** *optional check* — require `azp = H9F6QG5SzTKMv0tbmgxLj9LjG1EKVllA` so only tokens obtained through our SPA are accepted. Stricter, but rejects tokens other legitimate clients might obtain for the same API. **Recommendation: skip**, rely on audience; mention as a hardening option.
9. **Not checked:** `typ` (Auth0 sets `JWT` on both token kinds, so it doesn't distinguish them); `scope`/`permissions` (no per-route permissions in this app).

### 010d — JWKS source and caching
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. `createRemoteJWKSet` with jose defaults** | Cache 10 min; on unknown `kid`, refetch at most once per 30 s (limits abuse by tokens with random `kid`s); 5 s fetch timeout. |
| B. Same, tuned values | e.g. longer cache. No evidence we need it. |
| C. Static JWKS file committed to repo | No network dependency, but breaks on key rotation. |
**Recommendation: A.**
**JWKS URL / issuer / audience configuration:** from environment variables validated at startup (app refuses to start if missing), defaulting nothing. Rationale: BBL-17 (tests) may need to point verification at test keys *while running the same verification code* — the brief asks to keep the real validation path exercised. How tests get tokens is decided in BBL-17, not here.

### 010e — Failure responses
| Case | Recommended |
|---|---|
| Missing header / not `Bearer` / malformed / bad signature / wrong iss / wrong aud / expired | **401**, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` (RFC 6750, with `error="invalid_token"` when a token was present), **identical generic body** for all — the reason is logged server-side (never the token), not returned. |
| JWKS unreachable and no cached key | Options: **503 (recommended)** — honest "can't verify right now", avoids telling the SPA to re-login in a loop — or 401. |
Body shape follows the API error format decided in BBL-12.

### 010f — What the guard produces
Guard attaches a minimal typed principal `{ sub, scope }` to the request, exposed via a `@CurrentUser()` parameter decorator. User provisioning / `/userinfo` sync (ADR-009) is **not** in the guard — it's BBL-11, so token verification stays a pure, separately testable step.

### Tests that would prove it (for BBL-18)
No token → 401 · non-Bearer scheme → 401 · garbage token → 401 · `alg: none` → 401 · HS256 signed with the RSA public key → 401 · valid signature but wrong `iss` → 401 · ID token (`aud` = client id) → 401 · expired beyond tolerance → 401 · `nbf` in future → 401 · unknown `kid` → 401 · missing `sub` → 401 · token in query string only → 401 · valid access token → 200 · every registered route without token → 401.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
The BBL-10 proposal is ready for your decisions. The full text is ADR-010 in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md), marked **Proposed**, committed as `7ba12e1`. Nothing is implemented.

The BBL-10 card in Notion is now in **Needs decision** and lists the same questions as BBL-7. You can edit your answers there or reply here.

## The questions (my recommendation in bold)

| # | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 010a | JWT library | **`jose`**. It has no dependencies, is still maintained, and handles key rotation. I checked its source and it accepts our list-style `aud`. The passport route means 3 packages plus passport, and `passport-jwt` was last released in January 2025. |
| 010b | Where the guard applies | **One global guard that denies by default**, with `@Public()` to opt a route out. A forgotten route then returns 401 instead of being open. |
| 010b | Public routes | **None**, not even a health check. |
| 010c | Token checks | **Only from the `Authorization: Bearer` header** · **algorithm pinned to RS256** · **exact issuer** · **audience contains our API** (this is what rejects ID tokens) · **5 s clock tolerance** · **`sub` required** |
| 010c | Also require `azp` = our client id? | **No.** It would be optional hardening, worth mentioning if asked. |
| 010d | Signing keys (JWKS) | **jose's built-in defaults:** keys cached 10 min, an unknown `kid` refetched at most every 30 s, 5 s timeout. |
| 010d | Configuration | **Issuer, audience and JWKS URL from required environment variables.** The app won't start without them, and tests can point the same checking code at test keys. |
| 010e | Invalid token | **401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` and the same generic body for every failure.** The reason goes only to the server log, never the token. |
| 010e | Auth0's keys unreachable | **503.** It's our outage, not a bad token, so the SPA shouldn't send users back to log in. |
| 010f | What the guard passes on | **Only `{ sub, scope }` through `@CurrentUser()`.** Creating the user record and calling `/userinfo` stay in BBL-11. |

**Two points to be ready to explain:**
- **Why pin RS256?** It blocks `alg: none` and the HS256 attack where someone signs with the *public* key.
- **Why the 30 s refetch cooldown?** Without it, tokens with random `kid` values could make every request refetch Auth0's keys.

**Planned security tests (BBL-18):** no token, wrong scheme, garbage, `alg: none`, HS256 signed with the public key, wrong issuer, an ID token, expired, future `nbf`, unknown `kid`, missing `sub`, token only in the query string. All of these should return 401. A valid token should return 200, and every route should return 401 without a token.

Tell me your answers here or edit the card. I'll implement only after you decide.

input.content:
## Outcome (2026-09-17)
**Decision:** you accepted all ADR-010 recommendations.

### Files (backend/src/auth/)
- `auth.config.ts`: reads `AUTH_ISSUER`, `AUTH_AUDIENCE`, `AUTH_JWKS_URI`; throws at startup if any is missing or the URL is invalid.
- `token-verifier.ts`: the single place tokens are verified (jose `jwtVerify`) and errors are classified.
- `auth.guard.ts`: global guard. Reads the `Authorization` header, calls the verifier, turns results into 401/503.
- `auth.module.ts`: wires config, the remote JWKS (`createRemoteJWKSet`), the verifier, and `APP_GUARD`.
- `public.decorator.ts` (`@Public()`, unused), `current-user.decorator.ts` (`@CurrentUser()` → `{ sub, scope }`).
- `main.ts` loads `backend/.env` with Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile` (no new dependency).

### Logic — request walkthrough
1. Request hits the global `AuthGuard`. If the route is `@Public()`, allow (no route is).
2. Header must match `Bearer <token>` (scheme case-insensitive). Otherwise → 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
3. `TokenVerifier.verify` → jose checks: alg is RS256; finds the JWKS key by `kid`; verifies the signature; `iss` exact; `aud` contains the API; `exp`/`nbf` with 5 s tolerance; `sub` and `exp` present.
4. Success → `request.principal = { sub, scope }` → controller reads it via `@CurrentUser()`.
5. Token error → 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`, same body every time; reason logged (never the token).
6. Signing keys unavailable → 503 (our outage, not a bad token).

### Things the AI got wrong or nearly got wrong (good interview material)
1. **Outage misreported as bad token (avoided by reading jose's source).** jose throws a *generic* `JOSEError` when the JWKS URL returns non-200, `JWKSTimeout` on timeout, and a raw `TypeError` on network failure. "Catch jose errors → 401" would tell users to log in again during an Auth0 outage. Fix: classify by explicit error codes.
2. **Test helper bug.** `SignJWT.setIssuer/setAudience/setExpirationTime` run after the constructor and overwrote the "bad" claims tests passed in. 4 negative tests got 200, and the "expired within tolerance → 200" test passed for the wrong reason. 3. **Mutation testing found an untested check.** Deliberately removing each check: issuer, audience, tolerance, exp, and error classification were all caught. **Removing the RS256 pin broke nothing**, because jose already refuses `alg: none` and won't match an HS256 header to an RSA key. - "Every registered route → 401" sweep, and cross-user tests: BBL-18.
- Error body shape: BBL-12. User provisioning / `/userinfo`: BBL-11. CORS: frontend integration.

I built the auth guard with all your recommended choices. Every route now requires a valid Auth0 access token, and the 32 unit tests plus the e2e test pass, as do the build and lint.

It's committed as `3c07c29`, plus `ea82568`, which untracks a build file that slipped in. BBL-10 is Done in Notion with the details.

## How it works
Everything is in `backend/src/auth/`:
- **Global guard:** a request without `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] gets 401.
- **Token check** (`token-verifier.ts`, the only place tokens are checked, using jose):
  - RS256 only
  - exact issuer
  - audience list must contain our API
  - `exp` and `sub` required
  - 5-second clock tolerance
  - Auth0's signing keys fetched and cached automatically
- **Success:** controllers get `{ sub, scope }` through `@CurrentUser()`.
- **Bad token:** 401 with the same generic body every time. The reason goes to the server log, never the token.
- **Auth0's keys unreachable:** 503.
- **Missing `AUTH_*` settings:** the app refuses to start.

## What went wrong along the way (useful for AI_WORKFLOW.md and the interview)
1. **An Auth0 outage would have looked like a bad token.** From jose's source I found that when the key endpoint is down or returns an error, jose throws a *generic* error, not a JWKS-specific one. Catching all jose errors as 401 would log users out during an outage. I now sort errors by their exact codes.
2. **A test helper bug.** jose's `setIssuer`/`setAudience`/`setExpirationTime` silently replaced the bad claims my tests passed in. On the first run 4 "should reject" tests got 200. Worse, one "should accept" test passed for the wrong reason. Fixed.
3. **Mutation testing found a check with no real test.** I removed each check one at a time to see whether a test fails. Issuer, audience, tolerance, `exp` and error sorting were all caught. **Removing the RS256 pin broke nothing,** because jose already blocks `alg: none` and HS256-with-an-RSA-key on its own. The pin matters when a signing key doesn't declare its algorithm: a PS256 token signed with the real key would pass. I added a test for that case.
4. **That new test was misleading at first.** It crashed while creating its token, so it "caught" the removed pin only because it always failed. I noticed because it also failed on the unchanged code. After fixing it, it passes on the real code and fails without the pin ("expected 401, got 200").

## Checked by hand against the real tenant settings
- Curl requests with no token, a Basic credential, garbage, a forged HS256 token and `alg: none` → all 401 with the right headers.
- An unreachable key URL and an Auth0 URL that returns 404 → both 503.
- `AUTH_AUDIENCE` missing → the app won't start.

## Not tested yet
**A real Auth0 token against the running API.** All automated tests use keys I generated locally. One way to cover this is to extend `inspect-tokens.mjs`: after your login it would call `GET /` on the API with the real token, expecting 200, still without printing the token. That means one more login from you.

Also left for their own tasks: the error body format (BBL-12, currently Nest's default), creating the user record and calling `/userinfo` (BBL-11), and CORS.

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='DECISIONS.md'; s=open(p).read()
row="| 010 | API authentication guard (library, scope, checks, JWKS, errors) | Accepted — implemented | Developer (all agent recommendations) |"
assert row in s
s=s.replace(row,row+"\n| 011 | User provisioning, `/userinfo` sync, `GET /me` | **Proposed** — awaiting developer | — |")
s += r"""
## ADR-011 — User provisioning, profile sync, and `GET /me` (BBL-11)
**Status.** **Proposed** — awaiting developer decision. Nothing implemented.
**Already decided (inputs).** ADR-007: a `User` row keyed by Auth0 `sub`, created on the first authenticated request. ADR-009: `email`, `emailVerified`, `name` come from Auth0 `/userinfo` (server-side, caller's verified access token) on first sign-in and when older than 24 h. ADR-010f: `TokenVerifier` stays a pure verification step; controllers get identity via `@CurrentUser()`.
**Current schema.** `User(id uuid, auth0Sub unique, email?, emailVerified=false, name?, createdAt, updatedAt)`. No sync timestamp yet.

### 011a — Where provisioning runs
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. In `AuthGuard`, after `TokenVerifier` succeeds** | Guard calls `UserProvisioner.resolve(principal, token)` and puts the DB user on the request. Deterministic order, one place, every authenticated route has a user row. `TokenVerifier` remains pure and keeps its own tests. **Amends ADR-010f's wording** ("not in the guard") — the verifier is still separate, but the guard orchestrates both. |
| B. Global interceptor after the guard | Keeps the guard untouched. Nest always runs guards before interceptors, so order is safe, but auth now spans two classes and two places to skip `@Public()`. |
| C. Each controller calls `usersService.resolve()` | Explicit, but can be forgotten → a handler without an owner id. Fails open-ish. |
**Recommendation: A.**

### 011b — What controllers receive
`@CurrentUser()` returns `{ id, sub }` where **`id` is the `User.id` UUID used as `ownerId` everywhere**. Email/name are not on the request object (fetch via `/me` or the users service when needed, e.g. sharing), so handlers can't accidentally trust a stale or unverified email.
**Recommendation: `{ id, sub }`.** Alternative: include `email`, `emailVerified` for convenience.

### 011c — Creating the row safely under concurrency
A new user's SPA may fire several requests at once → two "create" attempts for the same `sub`.
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. Prisma `upsert` keyed on `auth0Sub`** | With a single unique field in `where` and no nested writes Prisma issues a native `INSERT … ON CONFLICT`, so parallel first requests can't create duplicates or throw. To be proven with a parallel-request test, not assumed. |
| B. `findUnique`, then `create`, catch unique violation (`P2002`) and re-read | Works, more code paths to test. |
**Recommendation: A**, with the parallel test.

### 011d — When `/userinfo` is called
Per ADR-009: user has never synced, or last sync > 24 h ago. **Schema change:** add `profileSyncedAt DateTime?` (null = never synced).
Concurrency after 24 h: several parallel requests may each call `/userinfo` once. **Recommendation: accept** (rare, bounded per user) rather than add an in-memory single-flight lock (doesn't work across multiple API instances anyway).

### 011e — When `/userinfo` fails
| Case | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **First sign-in**, Auth0 down / timeout / 5xx / 429 | (1) 503, user can't use the app until Auth0 recovers. (2) Create user with no email, `emailVerified=false`, `profileSyncedAt=null`; retry on the next request. | **(2)** — private features don't need email; sharing to this user is impossible until verified, which fails safe. |
| **Stale refresh** fails | (1) Keep stored values, don't bump `profileSyncedAt`, log warning, continue. (2) Set `emailVerified=false` until refresh succeeds (fail closed for sharing). | **(1)** — availability; the sharing risk window is "an email that stopped being verified during an Auth0 outage". Mention (2) as hardening. |
| `/userinfo` returns **401** for a token our guard accepted | (1) 401 `invalid_token` (Auth0 considers the session invalid). (2) Treat as outage. | **(1)** |
| `/userinfo` `sub` ≠ token `sub` | Should never happen. | **Reject → 401, log error.** |
| **Retry storm** while Auth0 is down and user never synced | Every request retries with a timeout → slow requests. | **3 s timeout** on the call; and don't retry for the same user more than once per **60 s** (`profileSyncAttemptedAt`, or in-memory). Needs your call: accept extra column, in-memory, or no backoff. |

### 011f — What is stored
- `email`: **trimmed and lower-cased** so sharing lookups (ADR-006a) are case-insensitive. Alternative: store as returned and compare case-insensitively in queries.
- `emailVerified`: `email_verified === true` only (missing → false).
- `name`: as returned.
- **Not stored:** `picture`, `nickname`, `updated_at`, anything else (data minimisation).
- If Auth0 returns no email → store `null`, `emailVerified=false`.

### 011g — `GET /me` response
| Option | Body |
|---|---|
| **A** | `{ id, email, emailVerified, name }` |
| B | A + `createdAt` |
| C | A + Auth0 `sub` |
**Recommendation: A.** `sub` is an external identifier the SPA doesn't need; `id` is the user's own id (not another user's), so exposing it is fine. Status `200`. No token → `401` (guard). Does not force a `/userinfo` refresh — same 24 h rule as every route.

### 011h — Configuration and HTTP client
- `AUTH_USERINFO_URI` as a **required env var** (consistent with ADR-010d; tests point it at a fake). Alternative: derive `issuer + "userinfo"`.
- Built-in `fetch` with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)`. No new dependency.
- Prisma: a `PrismaService` using `@prisma/adapter-pg` with required `DATABASE_URL`; app refuses to start without it.

### 011i — How it's tested (needs a DB, overlaps BBL-17)
- `UserInfoClient` is an injectable provider → tests override it with a fake (success, timeout, 401, 5xx, sub mismatch).
- DB tests run against `bookmarks_test`. **Decision needed now (pulls part of BBL-17 forward):** reset strategy.
  - **A. `prisma migrate deploy` once, then `TRUNCATE` all tables before each test; test files run serially.** Simple, realistic (real commits, real constraints). *Recommended.*
  - B. Wrap each test in a transaction and roll back — fast, but the request handling runs its own connection, so hard to make work through HTTP.
  - C. Unique random `sub` per test, never clean — no isolation guarantees.
- Planned tests: first request creates user + syncs; second request within 24 h doesn't call `/userinfo`; after 24 h it does; parallel first requests create exactly one row; each failure case in 011e; email lower-cased; picture not stored; `/me` shape; `/me` without token → 401.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git add DECISIONS.md && git commit -q -m "docs: propose ADR-011 user provisioning, /userinfo sync and GET /me (BBL-11)

Proposal only, no implementation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline | head -1

input.content:
## Proposal — ADR-011 (full text in DECISIONS.md)
### Decision questions (edit the [answer] brackets; agent recommendation shown)
- **011a Where provisioning runs:** in AuthGuard after token verification (verifier stays separate) / global interceptor / each controller? **[AuthGuard]** — note: amends ADR-010f wording.
- **011b What @CurrentUser() returns:** `{ id, sub }` (id = User.id used as ownerId) / also email + emailVerified? **[{ id, sub }]**
- **011c Creating the user row:** Prisma upsert on auth0Sub, proven by a parallel-request test / find-then-create with conflict retry? **[upsert + parallel test]**
- **011d Schema:** add `profileSyncedAt` (null = never synced)? **[yes]** · Parallel refreshes after 24 h: accept duplicates / add lock? **[accept]**
- **011e First sign-in, /userinfo down:** 503 / create user without email and retry next request? **[create without email]**
- **011e Stale refresh fails:** keep stored values + log / mark emailVerified=false until refreshed? **[keep + log]**
- **011e /userinfo says 401:** return 401 invalid_token / treat as outage? **[401]**
- **011e /userinfo sub ≠ token sub:** reject 401 + log error? **[yes]**
- **011e Retry storm while Auth0 down:** 3 s timeout + retry at most every 60 s via extra column / in-memory / no backoff? **[3 s timeout; your call on backoff]**
- **011f Email storage:** trim + lower-case / store as returned? **[lower-case]** · Store picture/nickname? **[no]**
- **011g GET /me body:** `{ id, email, emailVerified, name }` / + createdAt / + sub? **[{ id, email, emailVerified, name }]**
- **011h Config:** `AUTH_USERINFO_URI` required env var / derive from issuer? **[env var]** · `DATABASE_URL` required at startup? **[yes]**
- **011i DB test reset:** migrate once + TRUNCATE before each test, serial files / transaction rollback / random subs, never clean? **[migrate + truncate]**

### Logic — how to explain the recommendations
- **Guard orchestrates, verifier stays pure:** verification is still one separately tested class; the guard guarantees every authenticated request has a DB user before any handler runs, so a handler can't forget.
- **Controllers only get `{ id, sub }`:** handlers can't accidentally use a stale or unverified email for decisions.
- **Upsert:** a new user's SPA fires several requests at once; a native `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` avoids duplicate rows and unique-constraint errors. Proven with a test, not assumed.
- **Create without email on outage:** private features don't need an email. Sharing to that user stays impossible until verified, so it fails safe.

- **Don't store picture/nickname:** data minimisation; nothing uses them.
- **Truncate-based DB tests:** requests run on real connections with real constraints (the composite FK, cascades), which transaction-rollback tests can't easily reproduce through HTTP.

| 011f | What gets stored | **Email trimmed and lower-cased** for case-insensitive sharing lookups. **Don't store picture or nickname.** |
| 011g | `GET /me` body | **`{ id, email, emailVerified, name }`** |

message.content: what does 011e means?

content.text:
011e decides **what the API does when it can't get a user's email from Auth0.**

## Background
Your decision in ADR-009 was that the API gets the user's email and "verified" status by calling Auth0's `/userinfo` endpoint:
- the **first time** a user uses the app, and
- again when the stored copy is **more than 24 hours old**.

That call goes over the internet to Auth0, so sometimes it will fail. 011e decides what happens in each kind of failure.

## The five cases

**1. First sign-in, and Auth0 is down**
A brand-new user logs in (the token is fine), but `/userinfo` times out, so we don't know their email yet.
- **Option 1:** return 503, so the app doesn't work for them until Auth0 recovers.
- **Option 2 (recommended):** create their user record without an email and let them use the app. On their next request we try `/userinfo` again.
- **Why option 2 is safe:** bookmarks and collections don't need an email. The only feature that does is *receiving* a share, and that requires a verified email. Without one, nobody can share with them yet, so nothing leaks.

**2. Returning user, their 24-hour refresh fails**
We already have their email from yesterday, but today's refresh call fails.
- **Option 1 (recommended):** keep yesterday's email, log a warning, let the request through, and try again next time.
- **Option 2 (stricter):** mark their email "unverified" until a refresh succeeds, which blocks shares to them in the meantime.
- **The risk option 1 accepts:** say the user changed or un-verified their email in Auth0 during the outage. For a little longer, shares could still be sent to the old stored email.

**3. Auth0 says the token is invalid**
Our guard accepted the token (valid signature, not expired), but `/userinfo` answers 401. That usually means Auth0 ended that login session, for example after a logout elsewhere or a revoked session.
- **Recommended:** trust Auth0 and return 401, so the user logs in again.

**4. `/userinfo` returns a different user**
We call `/userinfo` with user A's token, and Auth0 returns `sub` = user B. This should never happen.
- **Recommended:** reject with 401 and log it as an error, rather than risk saving B's email on A's account.

**5. Retry storm**
Combine case 1 with an outage lasting minutes. The new user has no email yet, so **every** request tries `/userinfo` again, and each attempt waits for Auth0 to time out. The app feels slow for that user.
- **Timeout (recommended):** give up on each call after **3 seconds**.
- **Backoff (your call):** limit how often we retry for the same user:
  - **New column** (`profileSyncAttemptedAt`): at most one attempt per 60 s, remembered in the database.
  - **In memory:** same limit, but it resets when the server restarts and isn't shared between multiple servers.
  - **No backoff:** simplest. Each request may wait up to 3 s while Auth0 is down.

## What I need from you
Cases 1–4 have a recommendation you can accept or change. **Case 5 needs you to pick a backoff option.** For this app, **no backoff** is reasonable: outages are rare, and the 3 s timeout limits the damage. The new column is more robust but adds a column and more to test.

content.thinking: Confirmed the bug: Prisma only uses safe `ON CONFLICT` upserts when `update` has fields, so an empty `update: {}` falls back to a racy SELECT-then-INSERT (171/200 failures). Fixing it by making the update no-op with `update: { auth0Sub: sub }` so it always takes the atomic path.

## Outcome (2026-09-17)
**Decision:** all ADR-011 recommendations; for the retry storm (011e case 5) a **3 s timeout with no backoff**. You also asked for a plain-language explanation of 011e before deciding.

### Files
- `prisma/schema.prisma` + migration `20260917120000_user_profile_synced_at`: new `User.profileSyncedAt` (null = never synced).
- `src/prisma/`: `PrismaService` (Postgres via `@prisma/adapter-pg`; `DATABASE_URL` required).
- `src/auth/userinfo.client.ts`: calls Auth0 `/userinfo` with the caller's token; 3 s timeout; never throws; returns `ok` / `unauthorized` / `unavailable(reason)`.
- `src/auth/user-provisioner.ts`: the rules. `toProfile()` normalises email.
- `src/auth/auth.guard.ts`: after `TokenVerifier`, calls `UserProvisioner`; puts `{ id, sub }` on the request.
- `src/users/`: `GET /me` → `{ id, email, emailVerified, name }`.
- `test/support/`: shared token signer, DB reset + safety check, global setup (migrations).

### Logic — request walkthrough
1. Guard verifies the token (unchanged, BBL-10) → `sub`.
2. Provisioner looks up User by `auth0Sub`.
3. Synced less than 24 h ago → done, no network call.
4. Otherwise call `/userinfo`:
   - **ok**, same `sub` → upsert User with email (trimmed, lower-case), emailVerified (only if exactly `true`), name, `profileSyncedAt = now`.
   - **ok**, different `sub` → 401, log error, store nothing.
   - **unauthorized** → 401 `invalid_token`, change nothing.
   - **unavailable**, user exists → keep stored profile, don't bump sync time, log warning (retries next request).
   - **unavailable**, new user → create row with no profile (retries next request).
5. `request.user = { id, sub }` → controllers use `id` as `ownerId`.

### Bug the tests caught (strong interview story)
- **Symptom:** the e2e test "10 parallel first requests while /userinfo is down" got **9 × 500**.
- **Cause:** the proposal assumed Prisma `upsert` is an atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT`. It is **only if `update` has a field**. With `update: {}`, Prisma 7.10 silently does SELECT then INSERT, so concurrent requests collide on the unique `auth0Sub` (P2002).
- **Evidence:** probe of 200 parallel upserts per variant: `update: {}` → **171/200 failed**, no ON CONFLICT in SQL; non-empty update → **0/200**, ON CONFLICT used.
- **Also caught:** my first probe ran one round and showed "10 ok" by luck, and it truncated SQL logs at 110 chars, which could hide ON CONFLICT. Re-ran with full SQL and 20 rounds.
- **Fix:** `update: { auth0Sub: sub }` (same value). Putting `{}` back makes the test fail again.
- **Rule added to CLAUDE.md** so future agent sessions don't repeat it.

### Verification
- **Unit (`npm test`, 58):** UserInfoClient against a real local HTTP server (200, 401, 403/429/500/503, redirect not followed, invalid JSON, missing sub, timeout returns fast, connection refused, 3 s default); `toProfile` normalisation; guard passes sub + token to provisioner, skips it for invalid tokens, maps provisioner 401/500; config requires the new env var.
- **e2e with real Postgres (`npm run test:e2e`, 15):** first sign-in creates + syncs once; /me body shape; parallel first requests → 1 row (with and without /userinfo); no refresh within 24 h, refresh after 24 h, no refresh at 24 h minus 1 min; each failure case; /me without token → 401 and no row; two users get different ids and their own profiles; missing email_verified → false.
- **Mutation check:** 6 deliberate rule breaks, each made e2e fail.
- **DB safety:** dev DB untouched (0 users); the check refuses any database not named `bookmarks_test`.
- **Manual:** built app maps `/` and `/me`; `/me` without token → 401; missing `DATABASE_URL` / `AUTH_USERINFO_URI` → refuses to start.

### Not done
- `/me` with a **real Auth0 login** (would exercise the real `/userinfo`). Could reuse `inspect-tokens.mjs --api http://localhost:4000/me`.
- Pre-existing `supertest/types` type error in the scaffold e2e file (BBL-17).

5. `request.user = { id, sub }` → controllers use `id` as `ownerId`.

### Bug the tests caught (strong interview story)
- **Symptom:** the e2e test "10 parallel first requests while /userinfo is down" got **9 × 500**.
- **Cause:** the proposal assumed Prisma `upsert` is an atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT`. It is **only if `update` has a field**. With `update: {}`, Prisma 7.10 silently does SELECT then INSERT, so concurrent requests collide on the unique `auth0Sub` (P2002).
- **Evidence:** probe of 200 parallel upserts per variant: `update: {}` → **171/200 failed**, no ON CONFLICT in SQL; non-empty update → **0/200**, ON CONFLICT used.
- **Also caught:** my first probe ran one round and showed "10 ok" by luck, and it truncated SQL logs at 110 chars, which could hide ON CONFLICT. Re-ran with full SQL and 20 rounds.
- **Fix:** `update: { auth0Sub: sub }` (same value). Putting `{}` back makes the test fail again.
- **Rule added to CLAUDE.md** so future agent sessions don't repeat it.

### Verification
- **Unit (`npm test`, 58):** UserInfoClient against a real local HTTP server (200, 401, 403/429/500/503, redirect not followed, invalid JSON, missing sub, timeout returns fast, connection refused, 3 s default); `toProfile` normalisation; guard passes sub + token to provisioner, skips it for invalid tokens, maps provisioner 401/500; config requires the new env var.
- **e2e with real Postgres (`npm run test:e2e`, 15):** first sign-in creates + syncs once; /me body shape; parallel first requests → 1 row (with and without /userinfo); no refresh within 24 h, refresh after 24 h, no refresh at 24 h minus 1 min; each failure case; /me without token → 401 and no row; two users get different ids and their own profiles; missing email_verified → false.
- **Mutation check:** 6 deliberate rule breaks, each made e2e fail.
- **DB safety:** dev DB untouched (0 users); the check refuses any database not named `bookmarks_test`.
- **Manual:** built app maps `/` and `/me`; `/me` without token → 401; missing `DATABASE_URL` / `AUTH_USERINFO_URI` → refuses to start.

### Not done
- `/me` with a **real Auth0 login** (would exercise the real `/userinfo`). Could reuse `inspect-tokens.mjs --api http://localhost:4000/me`.
- Pre-existing `supertest/types` type error in the scaffold e2e file (BBL-17).

I built BBL-11 with your recommended choices and a 3-second timeout with no backoff. The auth guard now creates and syncs the user record after checking the token, and `GET /me` works. The 58 unit tests and 15 end-to-end tests against a real Postgres database pass.

It's committed as `d99f310`, and the BBL-11 card in Notion is moved to Done with a step-by-step walkthrough of a request.

## How it works
1. The guard checks the token as before, then looks up the user by `sub`.
2. If their profile was synced less than 24 hours ago, nothing else happens.
3. Otherwise the API calls Auth0's `/userinfo` (3-second timeout) and saves email (trimmed, lower-cased), verified status and name. The new `profileSyncedAt` column records when.
4. Failures follow your 011e decisions:
   - **Down on first sign-in:** create the user without an email and retry on the next request.
   - **Down on a refresh:** keep the stored values.
   - **Auth0 rejects the token:** 401.
   - **Different `sub` returned:** 401, with an error logged.
5. Controllers get `{ id, sub }`. `GET /me` returns `{ id, email, emailVerified, name }`.

## A real bug the tests caught
The test sending **10 simultaneous first requests while `/userinfo` is down** got **9 × 500**.
- **Cause:** the proposal assumed Prisma's `upsert` is a single atomic database statement. It is only when `update` contains at least one field. With `update: {}`, Prisma quietly reads and then inserts, so simultaneous requests collide on the unique `auth0Sub`.
- **Measured:** 200 simultaneous attempts per variant. Empty `update`: **171/200 failed**. Non-empty `update`: **0/200**, running as a single `INSERT … ON CONFLICT`.
- **My own probe was misleading at first:** one round showed "10 ok" by luck, and it cut SQL lines short enough to hide the `ON CONFLICT`. Fixed both and re-ran.
- **Fix:** pass a no-op update (`update: { auth0Sub: sub }`). Putting `{}` back makes the test fail again. The rule is now in CLAUDE.md for future sessions.

## Other checks
- **Mutation testing:** I broke 6 provisioner rules one at a time and each made the end-to-end tests fail.
  - no 24-hour cache
  - never refresh
  - no `sub` mismatch check
  - Auth0 rejection treated as an outage
  - stored profile wiped on a failed refresh
  - email not lower-cased
- **Test database safety:** tests empty the tables before each run, run one file at a time, and refuse any database not named `bookmarks_test`. Your dev database still has 0 users.
- **Manual:** the built app serves `/me`, returns 401 without a token, and won't start without `DATABASE_URL` or `AUTH_USERINFO_URI`.

## Not verified yet
- **`/me` with a real Auth0 login.** The tests fake `/userinfo`. Re-running `node scripts/inspect-tokens.mjs --api http://localhost:4000/me` would test Auth0's real `/userinfo` and the database write together, with one login from you.
- **The old `supertest/types` type error** from the Nest scaffold, left for BBL-17.

Do you want the real-login check on `/me` now, or go to BBL-12 (the API contract: error format, status codes, list and filter parameters)?

content.text: Nest 12 has a built-in `StandardSchemaValidationPipe` that works directly with zod 4, which is one of the options. Writing the BBL-12 proposal:

input.command:
cd ~/Documents/Chaipitch_Fullstack_BBL-Test && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='DECISIONS.md'; s=open(p).read()
row="| 011 | User provisioning, `/userinfo` sync, `GET /me` | Accepted — implemented | Developer (agent recommendations; chose no backoff in 011e) |"
assert row in s
s=s.replace(row,row+"\n| 012 | API contract: errors, validation, verbs, lists, filters (BBL-12) | **Proposed** — awaiting developer | — |")
s += r"""
## ADR-012 — API contract for `/collections`, `/bookmarks`, `/me` (BBL-12)
**Status.** **Proposed** — awaiting developer decision. Nothing implemented. Once accepted, the contract is written to `API_DESIGN.md` and endpoints/tests follow it. Sharing routes (`/shared/...`) are specified in BBL-15.
**Already decided (inputs).** UUID ids, malformed path id → 404 (004/004a); collection delete cascades, non-empty needs `?confirm=true` else 409 + count (005/005b); same-owner check + composite FK (005a); duplicate names allowed (007); 401/503 rules (010e); `@CurrentUser()` → `{ id, sub }` (011b); length limits: collection name 200, url 2048, title 500, notes 10 000 (007).
**Brief requires.** Both resources: get one, list, create, PUT, PATCH, delete, **filtering**; `GET /collections/:id/bookmarks`; `/me`. Suggested fields include `ownerId`.

### 012a — Error response body
| Option | Example |
|---|---|
| **A. RFC 9457 Problem Details** (`application/problem+json`) | `{ "type": "about:blank", "title": "Not Found", "status": 404, "detail": "Collection not found", "code": "collection_not_found" }`; validation adds `"errors": [{ "field": "url", "message": "must be an http(s) URL" }]` |
| B. Keep Nest default | `{ "statusCode": 404, "message": "Not Found", "error": "Not Found" }` — validation `message` becomes an array of strings |
| C. Custom envelope | `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": [...] } }` |
**Recommendation: A** — a published standard (easy to defend), one global exception filter formats every error (including 401/503 from the guard), stable machine-readable `code`. The 401 body stays identical for all auth failures (010e).

### 012b — Status codes
| Situation | Recommended |
|---|---|
| GET one / list, PUT, PATCH success | `200` with the resource / list |
| POST success | `201` with the resource + `Location: /collections/{id}` |
| DELETE success | `204` no body |
| Body/query validation failure, malformed JSON, unknown fields | `400` with `errors[]` |
| Not found, not yours, malformed path id | `404`, identical body |
| Delete non-empty collection without `?confirm=true` | `409` with `bookmarkCount` |
| No/invalid token · signing keys down | `401` · `503` |
**Question:** validation `400` (recommended — one code, common) or `422 Unprocessable Content` for well-formed JSON that fails rules?

### 012c — Validation approach
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. zod 4 schemas + Nest 12's built-in `StandardSchemaValidationPipe`** | One schema per body/query; `z.strictObject` rejects unknown keys by default; PATCH schema derived from PUT (`.partial()`); TypeScript types inferred from the schema, so validation and types can't drift. zod 4.6.5 (2026-09). |
| B. `class-validator` + `class-transformer` + `ValidationPipe({ whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted })` | Classic Nest tutorial approach; decorators on DTO classes; relies on decorator metadata; `class-transformer` last released 2022. Easy to forget `forbidNonWhitelisted` and silently strip fields. |
**Recommendation: A.**

### 012d — Unknown and server-owned fields in request bodies
`id`, `ownerId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or any unknown key in a body.
| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. Reject with 400** | Client learns immediately that `ownerId` can't be set; nothing silently ignored. |
| B. Silently strip | Lenient, but a client could believe it set `ownerId`. |
**Recommendation: A.**

### 012e — String input rules
- Strings are **trimmed**; empty after trimming → 400 for required fields.
- `notes`: empty after trimming → stored as `null`? **Recommendation: yes** (one representation for "no notes").
- `url`: absolute URL, scheme **`http` or `https` only** — rejects `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:` which would become XSS/abuse vectors when the frontend renders the link. Stored as given (no normalisation, no fetching). Max 2048.
- Max lengths enforced in validation → `400` (not a database error → `500`).

### 012f — PUT vs PATCH semantics
- **PUT = full replacement** of client-editable fields. Collection: `{ name }` required. Bookmark: `{ url, title }` required; `notes`, `collectionId` **optional and default to `null` when omitted** (omitting them clears them). No create-via-PUT: unknown id → 404.
- **PATCH = partial update.** Only provided fields change; `null` clears a nullable field (`notes`, `collectionId`); `null` on a required field → 400. **Empty PATCH body `{}` → 400** (recommended) or 200 no-op?

| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **A. ## Proposal — ADR-012 (full text in DECISIONS.md)

- **012a Error body:** RFC 9457 Problem Details / Nest default / custom envelope? **[RFC 9457 + `code` + `errors[]`]**

- **012d Unknown or server-owned fields in body (id, ownerId, createdAt…):** reject 400 / strip silently? **[reject 400]**
- **012e Strings:** trim; required-but-empty → 400; empty notes → null? **[yes]** · URL must be absolute http/https only? **[yes]**
- **012f PUT:** full replace, omitted notes/collectionId become null, unknown id → 404? **[yes]** · **PATCH:** partial, null clears nullable fields? **[yes]** · Empty PATCH `{}`: 400 / 200 no-op? **[400]**
- **012g `ownerId` in responses:** omit / include as brief suggests? **[omit, justify in API_DESIGN.md]** · `bookmarkCount` on collections? **[include]** · null fields always present? **[yes]**
- **012h Lists:** envelope + cursor pagination / limit+offset+total / bare array? **[envelope + cursor, limit default 50 max 100]** · Sorting: fixed createdAt desc / allow-listed `?sort=`? **[fixed]**
- **012i Filters:** collections `?name=` contains; bookmarks `?collectionId=<uuid|none>`? **[yes]** · bookmarks `?q=` title contains? **[your call]** · Unknown query params: 400 / ignore? **[400]**
- **012i Filter by a collectionId not yours / nonexistent:** 200 empty list / 404? **[200 empty]** · Malformed collectionId in query: 400 / 404? **[400]**
- **012j GET /collections/:id/bookmarks:** 404 if not yours/nonexistent/malformed; same list format + `q`? **[yes]**
- **012k Bookmark assigned to a collection not yours / nonexistent:** 400 with field error / 404? **[400]**
- **012l Race (bookmark added between 409 and confirmed delete):** accept + document / `?confirm=<count>`? **[accept]**
- **012m Non-JSON body:** 400 via validation (no 415)? **[yes]** · ETags/optimistic concurrency: skip? **[skip]** · OpenAPI/Swagger: skip / add? **[skip]**

### Logic — how to explain the recommendations
- **Problem Details:** a published standard with one global filter formatting every error, including auth errors. A stable `code` lets the frontend react without parsing messages.
- **zod:** one schema gives validation *and* types; strict objects reject unknown fields by default; the PATCH schema is derived from PUT, so they can't drift. Nest 12 has the pipe built in.

- **Bad collectionId on write → 400, not 404:** a 404 on `PATCH /bookmarks/:id` should only ever mean "that bookmark isn't yours"; a field error is unambiguous and still reveals nothing.

Write `API_DESIGN.md` from the accepted answers → implement BBL-13/14 against it → tests check the documented codes.

I recorded the real-login results, fixed the timestamp, and wrote the BBL-12 proposal. It's waiting for your decisions.

## 1. Recorded and fixed (`4de2f3a`)
- **Results recorded** in DECISIONS.md (ADR-011 notes), TENANT_FINDINGS.md, and the BBL-11 card in Notion.
- **Timestamp fix:** when a user is created, `createdAt` and `profileSyncedAt` now get the same timestamp, so a new user can never look "synced before created".
  - This isn't the database-clock approach I first mentioned. It fixes the same problem without raw SQL.
  - A new e2e assertion checks the order, and without the fix it failed 5 out of 5 runs.
- **Tests:** all 58 unit and 15 e2e pass.

## 2. The BBL-12 proposal: the API contract
It's ADR-012 in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md), marked **Proposed** (`7b1c348`). The BBL-12 card in Notion is in **Needs decision**, with the same questions to edit. Nothing is implemented. Once you decide, I'll write `API_DESIGN.md` from your answers, and the collections and bookmarks endpoints will be built against it.

| # | Question | My recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 012a | Error body format | **RFC 9457 Problem Details**, plus a `code` and a list of field errors |
| 012b | Status codes | 201 + `Location` for create · 204 for delete · **400** for validation (or 422?) · 404 for not found / not yours · 409 for delete without confirmation |
| 012c | Validation library | **zod 4 with Nest 12's built-in `StandardSchemaValidationPipe`** (found while researching). One schema gives both validation and types. |
| 012d | `ownerId` / `id` / unknown fields in a request body | **Reject with 400**, don't silently drop them |
| 012e | Text inputs | Trim · empty notes stored as `null` · **URLs must be `http`/`https` only** (blocks `javascript:` links) |
| 012f | PUT vs PATCH | PUT replaces the whole resource (omitted notes/collection become `null`) · PATCH changes only what's sent (`null` clears) · **empty PATCH → 400** |
| 012g | Response fields | **Leave out `ownerId`**, which the brief's suggested shape includes; the reason goes in API_DESIGN.md · **include `bookmarkCount`** on collections |
| 012h | Lists | **`{ data, nextCursor }` with cursor pagination** (limit 50, max 100) · fixed newest-first order |
| 012i | Filters | Collections `?name=` · bookmarks `?collectionId=<uuid\|none>` · `?q=` on title (**your call**) · unknown query params → 400 · filtering by someone else's collection → **200 with an empty list** |
| 012j | `GET /collections/:id/bookmarks` | 404 if not yours · same list format |
| 012k | Moving a bookmark into someone else's collection | **400 with a field error** (not 404) |
| 012l | Bookmark added between the 409 and the confirmed delete | **Accept it and document it** |
| 012m | Other | No 415 · no ETags · **skip Swagger** |

**Calls that need extra thought:**
- **Leaving out `ownerId` (012g)** goes against the brief's suggested shape, so it needs a written reason.
- **`?q=` (012i)** has no recommendation from me.
- **Malformed ids in query strings (012i)** get 400, while malformed ids in the path get 404.

Answer here or edit the card.
